meta.title: About MCPEmails and Asgeir Albretsen
meta.description: MCPEmails is built and run by Asgeir Albretsen, a software developer in Bergen, Norway: one person, a registered Norwegian business, and open source code.

hero.title: Who runs MCPEmails
hero.lead: You are giving an AI agent access to your mail. Here is who runs the service in between: one person, a registered business, code you can read.

who.title: Who I am
who.p1: My name is Asgeir Albretsen. I am a software developer in Bergen, Norway, with a BSc in Computer Technology from the University of Bergen. I build and run MCPEmails alone.

rows.role: IT consulting at BI Norwegian Business School

who.p3: I still work full time as a software developer elsewhere. MCPEmails is independent, self funded, and built in my own time.

why.title: Why I built it
why.p1: I wanted my own agents working my inbox. Every option I found wanted a copy of my mail first: sync it, index it, keep it in someone else's database for as long as the account exists. For a mailbox full of invoices, contracts and password resets, that is a lot to give up for something I only needed now and then.
why.p2: So I built the version I was willing to use. Mail is fetched live when your agent asks for it and dropped once the response is sent, so there is no stored copy. The only thing kept is the mailbox credential, encrypted at rest, because the next call needs it. I run my own mail through it every day.

trusting.title: What you are trusting
points: A named person. Me, not a support alias. If something goes wrong, you know whose name is on it.

A registered business. MCPEmails is operated by Albretsen Consulting, a Norwegian sole proprietorship registered in Enhetsregisteret at Brønnøysundregistrene. A sole proprietorship means personal liability.
Code you can read. The server is public on GitHub under AGPL-3.0, and the hosted service runs the same code.
trusting.entityNote: Full legal details are in the <terms>terms of service</terms> and the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

busFactor.title: If I get hit by a bus
busFactor.p1: One person running an email service is a real risk. I could fall ill, lose interest, or get hit by a bus. With a closed service, that would leave your agents wired into something nobody maintains.
busFactor.p2: That is what the licence is for. MCPEmails is open source under AGPL-3.0, and the hosted service runs the same server you can clone. If I stop, you clone the repository, bring the stack up with one command, point your agent at your own instance, and carry on. The tool names stay the same. Your credentials are yours, and your mail was never stored here.
busFactor.p3: Walk the self-host path once while everything is fine, so you know it works before you need it.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: There is no support queue. Your message arrives with me, and I answer it.
points: <hello>hello@mcpemails.com</hello> for the product, your account, billing, or a bug. Expect a reply within one business day.

<securityEmail>security@mcpemails.com</securityEmail> for vulnerability reports. Expect an acknowledgement within 24 hours. The disclosure process, including safe harbour, is on the <security>security page</security>.
I am in Bergen, Norway. A message sent late in the North American day is usually answered the next morning, European time.
